knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Gradient of a Function of Three Variables

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ given $f(x,y,z)=- 3 x^{2} + 3 y^{2} - z^{3}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=- 6 x \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=6 y \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=- 3 z^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}- 6 x \\ 6 y \\ - 3 z^{2}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ at $(-1,1,\frac{3 \pi}{4})$ given $f(x,y,z)=e^{x y} \cos{\left(x z \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=y e^{y x} \cos{\left(x z \right)} - z e^{y x} \sin{\left(x z \right)} \\ &=y e^{x y} \cos{\left(x z \right)} - z e^{x y} \sin{\left(x z \right)} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=x e^{y x} \cos{\left(x z \right)} \\ &=x e^{x y} \cos{\left(x z \right)} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=- x e^{y x} \sin{\left(x z \right)} \\ &=- x e^{x y} \sin{\left(x z \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}y e^{x y} \cos{\left(x z \right)} - z e^{x y} \sin{\left(x z \right)} \\ x e^{x y} \cos{\left(x z \right)} \\ - x e^{x y} \sin{\left(x z \right)}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=-1$, $y=1$, $z=\frac{3 \pi}{4}$ into these partial derivatives. Here $\cos\left(- \frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and $\sin\left(- \frac{3 \pi}{4}\right)=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(-1,1,\frac{3 \pi}{4})&=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 e} + \frac{3 \sqrt{2} \pi}{8 e} \\ f_{y}(-1,1,\frac{3 \pi}{4})&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 e} \\ f_{z}(-1,1,\frac{3 \pi}{4})&=- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 e}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(-1,1,\frac{3 \pi}{4})&=\begin{pmatrix}- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 e} + \frac{3 \sqrt{2} \pi}{8 e} \\ \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 e} \\ - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2 e}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ at $(-2,1,2)$ given $f(x,y,z)=\frac{2 x y z}{- x + y + z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the quotient rule in each coordinate, holding the other coordinates constant. The denominator is nonzero at the requested point.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{2 y x z + 2 y z \left(y - x + z\right)}{\left(y - x + z\right)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{2 x y z + 2 y z \left(- x + y + z\right)}{\left(- x + y + z\right)^{2}} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{- 2 y x z + 2 x z \left(y - x + z\right)}{\left(y - x + z\right)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{- 2 x y z + 2 x z \left(- x + y + z\right)}{\left(- x + y + z\right)^{2}} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{- 2 y x z + 2 y x \left(y - x + z\right)}{\left(y - x + z\right)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{- 2 x y z + 2 x y \left(- x + y + z\right)}{\left(- x + y + z\right)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{2 x y z + 2 y z \left(- x + y + z\right)}{\left(- x + y + z\right)^{2}} \\ \frac{- 2 x y z + 2 x z \left(- x + y + z\right)}{\left(- x + y + z\right)^{2}} \\ \frac{- 2 x y z + 2 x y \left(- x + y + z\right)}{\left(- x + y + z\right)^{2}}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=-2$, $y=1$, $z=2$ into these partial derivatives.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(-2,1,2)&=\frac{12}{25} \\ f_{y}(-2,1,2)&=- \frac{32}{25} \\ f_{z}(-2,1,2)&=- \frac{12}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(-2,1,2)&=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{12}{25} \\ - \frac{32}{25} \\ - \frac{12}{25}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ given $f(x,y,z)=x y z \ln{\left(x y z \right)}.$ Work where $x>0$, $z>0$, $y>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=z y \ln{\left(x z y \right)} + \frac{x z y}{x} \\ &=y z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=x z \ln{\left(x z y \right)} + \frac{x z y}{y} \\ &=x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=x y \ln{\left(x z y \right)} + \frac{x z y}{z} \\ &=x y \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}y z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x y \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right)\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{pmatrix}y z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 2\right) \\ x y \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}y z \\ x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x y \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}y z \\ x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 2\right) \\ x y \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}y z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x y \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right)\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}y z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 1\right) \\ x z \left(\ln{\left(x y z \right)} + 2\right) \\ x y\end{pmatrix}

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ at $(-2,\pi,-1)$ given $f(x,y,z)=e^{x z} \cos{\left(y z \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=z e^{x z} \cos{\left(z y \right)} \\ &=z e^{x z} \cos{\left(y z \right)} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=- z e^{x z} \sin{\left(z y \right)} \\ &=- z e^{x z} \sin{\left(y z \right)} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=x e^{x z} \cos{\left(z y \right)} - y e^{x z} \sin{\left(z y \right)} \\ &=x e^{x z} \cos{\left(y z \right)} - y e^{x z} \sin{\left(y z \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}z e^{x z} \cos{\left(y z \right)} \\ - z e^{x z} \sin{\left(y z \right)} \\ x e^{x z} \cos{\left(y z \right)} - y e^{x z} \sin{\left(y z \right)}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=-2$, $y=\pi$, $z=-1$ into these partial derivatives. Here $\cos(- \pi)=-1$ and $\sin(- \pi)=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(-2,\pi,-1)&=e^{2} \\ f_{y}(-2,\pi,-1)&=0 \\ f_{z}(-2,\pi,-1)&=2 e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(-2,\pi,-1)&=\begin{pmatrix}e^{2} \\ 0 \\ 2 e^{2}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ at $(3,1,1)$ given $f(x,y,z)=\ln{\left(\sqrt{x y z} \right)}.$ Work where $x>0$, $z>0$, $y>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=\frac{z y \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x z y}}}{\sqrt{x z y}} \\ &=\frac{1}{2 x} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=\frac{x z \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x z y}}}{\sqrt{x z y}} \\ &=\frac{1}{2 y} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=\frac{x y \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x z y}}}{\sqrt{x z y}} \\ &=\frac{1}{2 z}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{2 x} \\ \frac{1}{2 y} \\ \frac{1}{2 z}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=3$, $y=1$, $z=1$ into these partial derivatives.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(3,1,1)&=\frac{1}{6} \\ f_{y}(3,1,1)&=\frac{1}{2} \\ f_{z}(3,1,1)&=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(3,1,1)&=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{6} \\ \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ at $(0,2,-2)$ given $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} y^{2} - x z^{2} + 2 y z.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=2 x y^{2} - z^{2} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=2 x^{2} y + 2 z \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=- 2 x z + 2 y\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}2 x y^{2} - z^{2} \\ 2 x^{2} y + 2 z \\ - 2 x z + 2 y\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=0$, $y=2$, $z=-2$ into these partial derivatives.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(0,2,-2)&=-4 \\ f_{y}(0,2,-2)&=-4 \\ f_{z}(0,2,-2)&=4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(0,2,-2)&=\begin{pmatrix}-4 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ given $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + e^{x y z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=2 x z^{2} y^{2} + z y e^{x z y} \\ &=2 x y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=2 x^{2} z^{2} y + x z e^{x z y} \\ &=2 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=2 x^{2} z y^{2} + x y e^{x z y} \\ &=2 x^{2} y^{2} z + x y e^{x y z}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}2 x y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y^{2} z + x y e^{x y z}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: \begin{pmatrix}2 x y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ 4 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y^{2} z + x y e^{x y z}\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2 x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y^{2} z + x y e^{x y z}\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2 x^{2} y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ 4 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y^{2} z + x y e^{x y z}\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2 x y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y^{2} z + x y e^{x y z}\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}2 x y^{2} z^{2} + y z e^{x y z} \\ 4 x^{2} y z^{2} + x z e^{x y z} \\ 2 x^{2} y^{2} z\end{pmatrix}

question.:question/problem: Evaluate $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ at $(1,\frac{\pi}{4},-2)$ given $f(x,y,z)=\sin{\left(x y z \right)}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=z y \cos{\left(x z y \right)} \\ &=y z \cos{\left(x y z \right)} \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=x z \cos{\left(x z y \right)} \\ &=x z \cos{\left(x y z \right)} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=x y \cos{\left(x z y \right)} \\ &=x y \cos{\left(x y z \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}y z \cos{\left(x y z \right)} \\ x z \cos{\left(x y z \right)} \\ x y \cos{\left(x y z \right)}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute $x=1$, $y=\frac{\pi}{4}$, $z=-2$ into these partial derivatives. Here $\cos\left(- \frac{\pi}{2}\right)=0$ and $\sin\left(- \frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(1,\frac{\pi}{4},-2)&=0 \\ f_{y}(1,\frac{\pi}{4},-2)&=0 \\ f_{z}(1,\frac{\pi}{4},-2)&=0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(1,\frac{\pi}{4},-2)&=\begin{pmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find $\nabla f(x,y,z)$ given $f(x,y,z)=x^{z} + z^{y}.$ Work where $x>0$, $z>0$, $y>0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Hold the other two coordinates constant in each partial derivative. Apply the power, chain, or product rule to the factors that depend on the active coordinate.

$$
\begin{aligned}f_{x}(x,y,z)&=x^{z - 1} z \\ f_{y}(x,y,z)&=z^{y} \ln{\left(z \right)} \\ f_{z}(x,y,z)&=x^{z} \ln{\left(x \right)} + z^{y - 1} y \\ &=x^{z} \ln{\left(x \right)} + y z^{y - 1}\end{aligned}
$$

Assemble the partials in $x,y,z$ order:

$$
\begin{aligned}\nabla f(x,y,z)&=\begin{pmatrix}x^{z - 1} z \\ z^{y} \ln{\left(z \right)} \\ x^{z} \ln{\left(x \right)} + y z^{y - 1}\end{pmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
